content_units: You already have a strong base for   instructional design  : 7 years of teaching maps well to analysis, curriculum design, facilitation, assessment, and learner support. Your best-fit targets are   Instructional Designer  ,   Learning Experience Designer  ,   Curriculum Designer  ,   eLearning Developer (entry-to-mid)  , and   Learning Specialist   roles in Toronto or remote across Canada.
- Lead with   learning design  , not classroom teaching
- Target   corporate L&D, higher education, SaaS, healthcare, finance, and public sector
- Emphasize   measurable learning outcomes  , LMS administration, stakeholder collaboration, and digital content creation
- Present yourself as a   teacher who already designs learning systems  , not a beginner changing careers
Area   Your Current Strength   How to Reframe for ID/LXD Roles   Priority
Curriculum planning   Unit and lesson design   Learning design; curriculum architecture; backward design; outcome alignment   High
Assessment   Rubrics, formative/summative evaluation   Learning measurement; evaluation strategy; assessment design; Kirkpatrick-aware thinking   High
LMS use   Managing course materials and learner flow   LMS administration; course setup; learner experience optimization; reporting support   High
Workshop facilitation   Teacher/student sessions   Instructor-led training facilitation; stakeholder training; SME workshops   High
English teaching   Literacy, communication, feedback   Content clarity; learner-centered writing; editing; accessibility-minded communication   High
Video editing   Basic multimedia creation   eLearning media production; microlearning assets; storyboard-to-video execution   Medium
Classroom management   Running instruction and support   Project coordination; learner engagement strategy; change enablement   Medium
Resume shift that will work better
- To:   Instructional Designer   Learning Experience Designer   Curriculum & eLearning Specialist
- target audience flexibility: K-12, adult learning, employee training
Rename experience bullets to business-friendly language
- Created lesson plans for Grade 10 English
- Designed standards-aligned learning experiences with clear objectives, assessments, and differentiated content for diverse learners
- Facilitated engaging instructor-led learning for multiple learner groups, using formative feedback to improve completion and performance
- Administered LMS course spaces, organized digital learning assets, tracked learner progress, and supported consistent course delivery
Portfolio Projects That Will Make You Competitive
Option 1:   Corporate onboarding module     Show you can design for business outcomes, not just schools   Best first portfolio piece
- Build a 10-15 minute onboarding module for a fictional or volunteer-based company
- Include needs analysis, learner persona, storyboard, final module, and evaluation plan
- Focus on compliance, communication, or customer service
Option 2:   Blended workshop redesign     Converts your facilitation experience into L&D evidence   Strong for Learning Specialist roles
- Take a workshop you already ran and redesign it as pre-work + live session + post-session reinforcement
- Include facilitator guide, participant workbook, slides, and learner feedback approach
Option 3:   Microlearning series     Demonstrates concise digital design and multimedia skills   Good for remote hiring managers
- Create 3 short modules or videos on one topic
- Show scripting, editing, visual consistency, and measurable objectives
- Host with a simple portfolio site or Notion/Webflow page
Option 4:   Curriculum map + design document     Proves strategic thinking beyond slide-building   Useful for higher ed/public sector roles
- Build a sample curriculum blueprint with outcomes, activities, assessments, and accessibility notes
- Include a short rationale explaining design decisions
What each portfolio piece should show
Gaps to Close and 90-Day Search Roadmap
Skill gaps most likely to matter
For CAD 75,000+ roles, the biggest likely gaps are:
-   Corporate/adult learning language   rather than school-based language
-   Authoring tools   such as Articulate Storyline and Rise
-   Portfolio proof   of business-facing design work
- Familiarity with   accessibility standards   and basic   UX/LXD thinking
- Comfort with   needs analysis and stakeholder interviews
- Basic exposure to   learning metrics   and post-training evaluation

Days 1-30   Rebrand for ID/LXD   Rewrite resume and LinkedIn; collect 15-20 job postings; extract keywords; choose 2 target titles; start Storyline/Rise practice   New resume, optimized LinkedIn, target-role keyword bank

Days 31-60   Build proof   Complete 2 portfolio pieces; write short case studies; ask 3 peers for feedback; create portfolio site; draft tailored cover letter base   Live portfolio with 2 strong samples

Days 61-90   Run focused search   Apply to 8-12 well-matched roles per week; network with Toronto and Canadian L&D professionals; tailor resume per role; practice interviews and work-sample stories   Active pipeline, interview answers, application tracker
-   2-4 stretch roles   if they ask for 1-2 tools you can learn quickly
- For your background,   CAD 75,000+   is realistic if you target:
- higher ed roles with digital learning scope
- It may be harder in pure entry-level eLearning production roles unless your portfolio is strong
